learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will understand how to shift focus between the doer of an action and the receiver by confidently converting sentences between Active and Passive voice across different tenses.]
warm_up_hook: 🎬 In a movie scene, the camera focuses on the most important action. Active voice puts the spotlight on the 'Doer' (the hero). Passive voice shifts the camera to focus entirely on the 'Receiver' of the action. Time to direct our sentences! 🎥

lesson_modules.teaching_content: In Active Voice, the Subject does the action (Subject -> Verb -> Object). In Passive Voice, the Object becomes the Subject and receives the action. The original 'doer' is moved to the end with the word 'by' (or removed entirely).
examples_or_templates: Active: The dog (Subject/Doer) chased the cat (Object/Receiver).
Passive: The cat (New Subject) was chased by the dog.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: To form the passive voice, you MUST use a form of the 'to be' verb matching the tense of the active sentence (is, are, was, were, been, being) + the Past Participle (V3) of the main verb.
examples_or_templates: Present Simple Passive: The letter IS WRITTEN.
Past Simple Passive: The letter WAS WRITTEN.
Present Continuous Passive: The letter IS BEING WRITTEN.

lesson_modules.module_title: 🕵️‍♂️ When to Use the Passive Voice
lesson_modules.teaching_content: We don't always use passive voice just for fun. Use it when the doer of the action is unknown, unimportant, or obvious. It is also highly preferred in scientific writing, lab reports, and formal news.
examples_or_templates: Unknown Doer: My bicycle was stolen! (I don't know who did it).
Scientific/Formal: The chemical was heated to 100 degrees Celsius.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the correct passive voice form of: 'The mechanic is repairing my car.'
options: My car is repaired by the mechanic.
My car was repairing the mechanic.
My car is being repaired by the mechanic.
My car has been repaired by the mechanic.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: My car is being repaired by the mechanic.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Why might an author choose to say 'Mistakes were made' instead of 'I made mistakes'?
options: To emphasize who made the mistakes.
To avoid taking direct responsibility (hiding the doer).
Because it is an active voice sentence.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: To avoid taking direct responsibility (hiding the doer).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Convert this sentence into passive voice: 'Shakespeare wrote Hamlet in 1599.'
subjective_practice.hint: Make 'Hamlet' the subject, use the past tense 'to be' verb, and add 'by Shakespeare'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Convert this passive sentence back to active voice: 'The new policy has been announced by the principal.'
subjective_practice.hint: Put the 'principal' back in the driver's seat as the subject doing the action.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🔬 The Science Reporter
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write a 4-step process on 'How to make a cup of tea' or 'How to plant a seed'. You must write the entire process using ONLY the Passive Voice (e.g., 'First, the water is boiled...'). No 'I' or 'You' allowed!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Active voice focuses on WHO does the action. Passive voice focuses on WHO/WHAT receives the action.
⭐ The golden rule for Passive Voice is: Verb 'to be' + Past Participle (V3).
⭐ Use the passive voice for scientific writing, or when the doer is unknown, obvious, or unimportant.
